Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

android.head: Where installs come from is shifting toward Paid Install (+5.8% vs -15.4% for installs overall).
android.body: Paid Install (YMK · US) was 3,918, +5.8% against last week, while total installs moved -15.4% — a difference of +21.1 percentage points. Paid Install is now 61.0% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

android.head: App Total New User is moving faster than the other steps (+6.6% vs about -15.4%).
android.body: App Total New User is +6.6% while the other steps are all moving about -15.4% — a gap of +22.0pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

ios.head: App Total Revenue -3.2% — down in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (-3.7%).
ios.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is -3.2%, and App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -3.7% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (this week vs last week): Subscription -2.6%, Pay as you go -28.3%. The drop was already visible in new subs a week ago, so lifting new subs now is what turns revenue around next week.

ios.head: App Total Revenue -3.2% — down mainly in Subscription (-2,827, -2.6%).
ios.body: App Total Revenue (YMK · US) was 105,576, against 109,051 for last week (-3,475). By purchase type: Subscription -2,827 (-2.6%), Pay as you go -647 (-28.3%). Pay as you go is 1.6% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

ios.head: App Total Install -5.5% — Paid Install is behind most of it (-975, -5.8%).
ios.body: App Total Install (YMK · US) was 24,051, against 25,463 for last week — a change of -1,412. Where that came from: Paid Install -975 (-5.8%), Organic Install -397 (-5.5%), SEO Install -45 (-7.4%). Paid Install moved the most on its own (-975, -5.8%) and is now 65.9% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

ios.head: All the funnel steps are moving together (down about -7.2%) — nothing out of step.
ios.body: New User, Install and New Subs are all moving by roughly the same amount (about -7.2%, none more than 5 percentage points away). Nothing is out of step for this selection.

ios.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
ios.body: App Total New Subs is -9.6% and App Total Install is -5.5%; the gap between them (-4.1pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

insights.title: Revenue vs new subs — App Total Revenue -3.7% — down in line with the new subs signed up 7 days earlier (-7.6%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue this week vs last week is -3.7%, and App Total New Subs last week vs the week before was -7.6% — both moved the same way. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (this week vs last week): Subscription -3.3%, Pay as you go -10.0%. The drop was already visible in new subs a week ago, so lifting new subs now is what turns revenue around next week.

insights.title: Revenue by purchase type — App Total Revenue -3.7% — down mainly in Subscription (-18,489, -3.3%).
insights.body: App Total Revenue was 577,102, against 599,046 for last week (-21,945). By purchase type: Subscription -18,489 (-3.3%), Pay as you go -3,455 (-10.0%). Pay as you go is 5.4% of revenue. Subscription is the recurring part fed by new subs about a week earlier; look at new subs and renewals.

insights.title: Purchase type by app — Subscription revenue is falling most in YMK (-5.7%), while YCV grows (+2.8%).
insights.body: By app: the biggest Subscription fall is YMK -15,340 (-5.7%, about 45% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in YMK -1,413 (-28.0%); YCV relies most on Pay as you go (14% of its revenue vs 5.4% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YCP is turning installs into New Subs better than usual (+10.2% vs Install +1.6%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCP New Subs +10.2% vs Install +1.6% (better than its installs); YMK New Subs -6.7% vs Install +0.1% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Revenue -3.7% is mostly YMK — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Revenue moved -3.7% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -3.7%, YMK -6.1%, YCP -2.1%, YCV +2.5%). YMK accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Purchase type by country — Subscription revenue is falling most in JP (-16.9%), while US grows (+1.6%).
insights.body: By country: the biggest Subscription fall is JP -4,862 (-16.9%, about 6% of revenue); Pay as you go moved most in JP -1,416 (-14.7%); JP relies most on Pay as you go (25% of its revenue vs 5.4% overall). Subscription is the recurring revenue that new subs feed; Pay as you go is one-off spend.

insights.title: Which country — US is out of line with every other country on App Total New User (-7.5% vs -1.8%).
insights.body: For All App, App Total New User in US is -7.5% while all countries together are -1.8% — a gap of -5.7pp. US is about 41% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — CA turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (18.5% vs 10.5% overall).
insights.body: In CA, 18.5% of installs turn into new subs, versus 10.5% across all markets and apps (+8.0pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. CA is about 2% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is +5.2% this period.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-7.9% vs -0.5% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 13,228, -7.9% against last week, while total installs moved -0.5% — a difference of -7.4 percentage points. SEO Install is now 6.4% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..

insights.title: Next period outlook — No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -0.5% and App Total Install is -0.5%; the gap between them (+0.0pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
